newsitem.title: MEXICO: Demonstrators hurt in two incidents in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Demonstrators hurt in two incidents in Mexico.

text.p: Political violence hit two southern Mexican states on Saturday injuring several people, officials said on Sunday.
In one incident police removed protesters blocking a road in the southern state of Oaxaca, injuring at least five members of the opposition Party of the Democractic Revolution (PRD).

In the state of Chiapas, seven Indian protesters were also injured in a clash on Saturday, after about 800 supporters of the ruling Revolutionary Institutional Party (PRI) tried to block about 1,500 backers of the rebel group, the Zapatista Army for National Liberation (EZLN), officials said.

The EZLN supporters were marching to show their backing for members of a local municipality and to protest against a fact finding mission by a group trying to negotiate a peace deal between the rebels and the government.

In Oaxaca, The president of the municipality of Juchitan, Roberto Lopez Rosado, told Reuters that at least five people were hurt there, including two with gunshot wounds, and a one-year old child made ill by tear gas.
The state government said 10 people were detained, and two people were slightly injured.
Members of the left-wing PRD had blocked a highway for the past 17 days, protesting the arrest of a party member accused of embezzlement.
